translation: The Blessed Lord said: Hear now, O Partha, how by anchoring your mind entirely upon My divine reality, practicing constant Yoga, and taking absolute refuge in Me, you can understand Me fully and thoroughly, completely free from any shadow of doubt.

I shall unfold to you in complete, exhaustive detail this profound theoretical knowledge (Jnana), along with its direct empirical verification (Vijnana). Once you have mastered this science, absolutely nothing else remains to be known in this world.

Among thousands of human beings, barely an isolated individual strives seriously to attain spiritual perfection. And among those rare, dedicated seekers who actively strive and achieve standard proficiency, scarcely one truly understands My divine nature in its ultimate essence.

Earth (solid matter), Water (liquidity), Fire (energy), Air (gaseous states), Ether (space), Mind (sensory processing center), Intellect (discriminating faculty), and Ego (individualized identity)—these eight elements constitute the structured classification of My lower material nature (Apara Prakriti).
simple_explanation: This verse highlights the scientific precision of Vedic cosmology. The first five elements represent the five fundamental states of matter and energy. Mind, Intellect, and Ego are included as subtle physical variables, anticipating modern physics' understanding that thoughts and individual memory are fields of energy operating within the material matrix.

translation: This is merely My lower, material nature, O mighty-armed warrior! Distinct from this, know My higher, transcendent nature (Para Prakriti), which manifests as the conscious life- principle (Jiva-bhuta) by which this entire universe is animated and sustained.

Understand clearly that all created beings emerge from the interaction of these two aspects of My nature. I am the sole origin from which this entire cosmos projects, and I am the ultimate dissolution into which it collapses.

There is absolutely nothing superior or independent beyond Me, O Dhananjaya! This entire universe is tightly woven and suspended upon My divine reality, exactly like a cluster of precious gems threaded along a single inner string (sutre mani-gana iva).

I am the essential taste within water, O son of Kunti; I am the brilliant radiance within the moon and the sun; I am the primordial, sacred syllable Om reverberating throughout all the Vedas; I am the sound-carrying capacity within space; and I am the raw grit, masculinity, and virtue (paurusham) within human beings.
simple_explanation: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to view the world through a spiritual lens. God is not an isolated ruler hiding in a distant heaven; He is the underlying essence that gives everything its specific quality. Water's identity is its ability to quench thirst (rasa); human identity is the capacity to act courageously (paurusha). When you look at these essential attributes, you are looking directly at the Divine.

translation: I am the pure, pristine fragrance within the earth; I am the consuming heat within the fire; I am the vital life-force (jivanam) pulsing through all living creatures; and I am the intense focus and self-discipline within ascetics (tapasvishu).
Know Me, O Partha, to be the eternal, primeval seed (bi-jam) from which all living beings sprout. I am the intelligence of the highly intelligent, and I am the splendid glory of the magnificent.

I am the physical strength of the strong when it is completely purged of personal lust and selfish attachment (kama-raga-vivarjitam). And within all living creatures, O foremost of the Bharata dynasty, I am that natural desire and drive (Kama) which operates in complete harmony with righteousness and social order (Dharma).

Know that all mental states and phenomena—whether characterized by pure goodness (Sattva), restless passion (Rajas), or dark inertia (Tamas)—emanate directly from My cosmic law. Yet, mark this boundary carefully: I am not dependent upon them or trapped inside them; rather, they are entirely contained and suspended within Me.

Deluded and blinded by these three modifications born of nature’s qualities, this entire world fails to perceive Me, who stand completely independent above these attributes as the absolute, immutable reality.

For this divine illusion of Mine (Maya), constructed out of the three modes of material nature, is extraordinarily difficult to cross over. But those rare souls who surrender themselves exclusively unto Me easily cross beyond this illusion.
simple_explanation: Maya does not mean that the physical world is a literal optical illusion or a non-existent dream. In Vedic grammar, Maya refers to the intricate, multi-layered mask of material properties that conceals the underlying Divine Presence. When a person falls in love with the temporary, outer forms of nature (wealth, power, or family prestige), he gets trapped in attraction and aversion. But when he shifts his focus to the permanent Divine source, the deceptive power of the mask automatically dissolves.

translation: The wicked evildoers, the dull-witted fools, and the lowest among men do not seek refuge in Me. Their discrimination has been completely stolen by this cosmic illusion, and they align themselves with the destructive, demonic nature (asuram bhavam).

Four distinct classes of virtuous people turn to worship Me, O Arjuna, foremost of the Bharata dynasty: the distressed individual crying out for relief (arta), the seeker searching for ultimate truth (jijnasu), the striver seeking material success (artharthi), and the wise sage of realized vision (jnani).

Of these, the wise sage (Jnani) who is permanently integrated in Yoga and single-mindedly devoted to the Absolute stands supreme. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise person, and he is equally dear to Me.

All these classes of devotees are undoubtedly noble and generous. But I look upon the wise person as My very own Self—such is My definitive view. For, with his faculties fully integrated in Yoga, he anchors his entire life securely upon Me alone as his highest, absolute destination.

At the culmination of multiple lifetimes of intense spiritual evolution, the person of true wisdom finally surrenders unto Me, realizing that the all-pervading Divine Presence (Vasudevah) constitutes everything that exists. A magnificent, expanded soul (Mahatma) of this caliber is exceedingly rare to find in this world.

But those individuals whose evaluation has been blinded by endless material cravings (kamaih), driven helplessly by their own lower psychological conditioning, turn to worship transient worldly forces or lesser deities, binding themselves to rigid, superficial rituals designed for specific material rewards.
Whichever lesser form or limited manifestation a devotee desires to worship with genuine faith, I honor that impulse and stabilize his faith in that specific direction.

Endowed with that reinforced faith, he engages in the worship of that limited entity and successfully obtains his desired rewards. But let it be understood that those material rewards are actually orchestrated and allocated by Me alone through cosmic laws.

However, the rewards obtained by these short-sighted people of small intelligence (alpa- medhasam) are temporary and perishable. Those who worship limited cosmic forces merge into those limited forces, whereas My devotees ascend directly to My eternal, absolute presence.

The ignorant, lacking intellectual depth, think that I was originally an unmanifest human soul who has recently assumed a temporary physical personality (vyaktim-apannam). They are completely blind to My supreme, immutable, and incomparable transcendent reality.

I am not casually visible to everyone, veiled as I am by My creative power of illusion (Yoga- maya). This deluded world fails to recognize Me as the unborn, undying, and unchangeable Reality behind all passing forms.

I know perfectly all living beings that have passed away in the ancient history, all that are actively existing in the present era, and all that are yet to come in the distant future, O Arjuna! But scarcely an isolated individual truly understands My ultimate reality.

By the powerful delusion of dualities arising directly from attraction and aversion (iccha- dvesha-samutthena), O descendant of Bharata, all created beings fall into deep delusion right from their very birth, O scorcher of foes!

But those virtuous individuals of noble deeds whose sins have been completely eliminated, break free from the blinding delusion of dualities and serve Me with unswerving, iron-clad determination (dridha-vratah).

Those who take absolute refuge in Me and strive diligently to win liberation from the cycle of decay and death (jara-marana-mokshaya), understand fully that Absolute Brahman, they possess complete knowledge of the inner Self (Adhyatma), and they comprehend the total architecture of action (Karma).

Those who recognize Me as the governing principle behind the material realm (Adhibhuta), the cosmic powers (Adhidaiva), and the spirit of sacrifice (Adhiyajna)—their minds remain integrated in Yoga, and they retain clear, unclouded awareness of Me even at the critical hour of death (prayana-kale).
